problem: Combine internet reach with media content.
title: AOL and Time Warner merge in a deal valued at about $165 billion
context: AOL used its high-valued stock to buy Time Warner at the peak of the dot-com boom.
decision_made: Merge, valuing Time Warner at about $164.75 billion with a combined market value near $350 billion.
action_taken: Completed the merger and reported results as AOL Time Warner.
observed_outcome: The company recorded write-downs of about $99 billion and reported a fiscal 2002 net loss of $98.7 billion, described as the largest annual loss in corporate history. Reports tie it to the dot-com bust and falling advertising.
lessons: A deal priced on a bubble valuation can destroy value when the underlying business weakens.
limitations: The write-down is a non-cash goodwill charge, not a cash loss. Deal and loss figures differ by source and whether debt is included.

claims.claim_text: AOL agreed to acquire Time Warner in a deal valuing Time Warner at about $164.75 billion.
Fortune's retrospective described the merger as failed and said advertising dollars evaporated.
